newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse seen taking cue from the U.S.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse seen taking cue from the U.S.

text.p: Belgian shares pushed higher on Friday aided by a stronger but volatile Dow Jones.
Dealers expected the Brussels Bel-20 share index to hover around present levels in coming days as investors await the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee's meeting next week for direction.
The blue-chip Bel-20 index closed up 0.28 percent at 2,051.54, with a moderate 2.86 billion francs volume of Belgian shares traded.
"The U.S. is a major factor right now. It's very wild over there. That is a major reason of why Brussels could fall back," one trader said.

"There is still consolidation here and this will probably continue in the beginning of next week. We have to wait until February 5 for new direction," said trader Paul de Lophem at brokerage Mignon, Hanart, Declerck.
On February 4-5 the FOMC, which sets U.S. interest rate policy, will meet. Some analysts fear it may raise rates to counter the threat of inflation.

A U.S. interest rate hike would put pressure on the Belgian stock market, still at record levels, and encourage investors, fearing the rate cycle in Europe will soon turn up as well, to look for alternative investments and head into cash.

One trader said some investors were likely to move out of U.S. stocks if Wall Street continued to stay volatile and invest instead in European equity markets as 1997 was expected to show growth in the near future.
Cement maker CBR was the Bel-20's main gainer, up 3.55 percent, at 3,350 francs recovering from recent profit-taking.
Investors jumped back into the stock as it is seen as a stock with strong earnings potential in 1997.
Electronics firm Barco ended up 2.2 percent at 5,660 francs, breaking an important 5,500 resistance level.
"Barco is moving to new heights after breaking the resistance level at 5,500, so the sky's the high for Barco," one trader said.
Retailer Delhaize gained 2.08 percent to 1,965 francs after recent profit-taking.
But some dealers said the stock had also fallen because a major U.S. investment bank had recommended investors switch to buy shares in Delhaize's U.S. unit Food Lion.
Elsewhere the banking sector suffered falls, with Generale Bank down 1.05 percent to 11,750 francs and Kredietbank down 1.26 percent to 11,775 francs.
